questions.question: When should you NOT point your wheels straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. If hit from behind, this prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill, turn your wheels so your car won't roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Are hidden in the truck's blind spots or so close the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths of space between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are hidden in the truck's blind spots or so close the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars disappear into a truck's or bus's blind spots. They are also areas where cars are so close to the larger vehicle that the driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "no zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Watch for trains coming from multiple directions.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from any direction. Also watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and hazmat trucks.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked cars to give more room to moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or car to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked cars. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their car before seeing you.

questions.question: What describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: Other drivers will always do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting other drivers to make mistakes and being ready to respond safely.

questions.question: You are behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane since the motorcycle is small and doesn't use the whole lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give it a full lane. Never share the same lane. Moving back to your original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When bright headlights are coming toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below the headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded at night, do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster. You should slow down for curves, hills with limited sight distance, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line next to your lane. This means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns here.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center, you can pass if the broken line is on your side and no oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
Your lane must turn right.
You can only turn right on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs have a fluorescent yellow-green background. They alert you to upcoming hazards, including curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What are crosswalks?

options.text: Always marked with pavement lines.
Either marked with lines or not marked at all.
Never marked with lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either marked with lines or not marked at all.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist with or without painted lines. You must stop at any crosswalk to let pedestrians cross.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause your car to hydroplane. At what speed can hydroplaning start?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. Below 35 mph, most tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away as well. Your tires may lose grip and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if a tire blows out. Hold the steering wheel tightly and take your foot off the gas. Let the car slow down on its own. Apply the brakes gently when safe. Wait until the car has slowed significantly before moving to the shoulder.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when no traffic is coming from the other direction.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Drive a little faster.
Be ready for anything.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected changes. Drive slowly and carefully to stay safe and protect workers.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only after a crash.
After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
Only when stopped for a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your insurance proof and license to an officer when asked, whether after a traffic stop or a crash.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
Passing on the right is allowed when the road ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is allowed when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is allowed when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass on the left when no traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from:

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The middle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: Start a left turn from a one-way street in the far left lane.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The highest safe speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed allowed. You can drive slower than this speed, but you cannot drive faster. Adjust your speed based on road and weather conditions.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous because it uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even good drivers increase their crash risk when using a phone.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass only from your direction.
No one can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Do not go forward.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: You must stop for them.
You do not have to stop.
Honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop for them.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally. You must stop for them.

questions.question: At an intersection where all four corners have stop signs, give the right-of-way to:

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: Drivers should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the right goes first.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a curved ramp going downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can make your car skid.
